title: Hacking Web Applications

objectives.text: Describe web application architecture (tiers, HTTP methods and status codes, cookies and sessions, same-origin policy, CORS, SOAP/REST/GraphQL) and tell encoding apart from encryption
Name the OWASP Top 10:2025 categories, map them to the 2021 list, and give the OWASP Cheat Sheet countermeasure for each
Recognize XSS, CSRF, SSRF, path traversal, command injection, XXE, deserialization, clickjacking and session fixation from a request, response or log clue
Explain what a web shell is (ATT&CK T1505.003) and list the host, file and log signs that reveal one
Put the web application testing phases in order and match each tool (Burp Suite modules, ZAP, Nikto, WhatWeb, wafw00f, gobuster, ffuf, WPScan) to its purpose
Name the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) risks, tell BOLA from BFLA, and describe how each shows up in API traffic
Explain how webhooks work and how a receiver verifies them (HMAC signature, timestamp tolerance, delivery IDs, SSRF limits)
Choose the right control for a web attack: output encoding, CSP, anti-CSRF tokens, cookie flags, security headers, rate limiting, WAF (models, modes, virtual patching)
Place secure SDLC practices in order (NIST SSDF, OWASP SAMM and ASVS, threat modeling, SAST/DAST/IAST/SCA, SBOM, logging and alerting)

readingMap.why: HTTP methods, status codes, cookie flags and encoding schemes appear inside other questions; learn the tables, skip long architecture descriptions.
The largest block of questions: an attack described in one sentence, and you name it or its fix. Learn the one clue per attack and both OWASP Top 10 editions.
Phase order and tool-to-purpose matching (Burp modules, ZAP scans, directory brute forcers, fingerprinting tools) are frequent tool questions.
v13 added APIs and webhooks: know the OWASP API Top 10 2023 by number and how webhook signatures stop forged deliveries.
Scenario questions ask for the best control; know which header, cookie flag or SDLC practice fixes which attack, and what a WAF can and cannot do. Skim vendor tool lists.

labs.name: Walk the OWASP Top 10 in OWASP Juice Shop
labs.skill: Running a deliberately vulnerable app locally, proxying it through ZAP or Burp and recognizing access control, XSS and misconfiguration findings; reading the official companion guide for the fixes

labs.name: PortSwigger Web Security Academy topic labs
labs.skill: Recognizing XSS, CSRF, SSRF, access control and API flaws in legal training labs, then writing the matching OWASP countermeasure

labs.name: Map the API Top 10 in OWASP crAPI
labs.skill: Mapping each OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) risk to an endpoint in a local, intentionally broken API

labs.name: Baseline-scan and harden a local app
labs.skill: Running the ZAP baseline (passive) scan against an app you own, then adding CSP, HSTS, nosniff and cookie flags and re-scanning

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a new developer why changing /api/orders/1001 to /api/orders/1002 should return 403, which OWASP lists call this flaw, and what single check in the code prevents it.
Tell the difference between reflected XSS, stored XSS and CSRF using one short story each, and say which control stops each one.
Your team receives payment events by webhook. Explain how you make sure a delivery really came from the provider, is not a replay, and cannot be abused to reach your internal network.
